statement: theorem graded_kernel_internal (R : Type u) (M : Type v) [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] : DirectSum.IsInternal (fun n : ℕ => ((TensorAlgebra.ι R : M →ₗ[R] TensorAlgebra R M).range ^ n).comap (LinearMap.ker (algHom R M).toLinearMap).subtype)

source.place: Algebra, Section 00DM (section-tensor-algebra, line 2165): T(M) is the direct sum of the T^n(M) with T^n * T^m in T^{n+m}; Sym(M) is the quotient of T(M) by the two-sided ideal generated by the degree-2 elements x (x) y - y (x) x, and Sym^n(M) is the image of T^n(M) (the text writes 'the image of a pure tensor x_1 (x) ... (x) x_n in Sym^n(M)'); the grading of the quotient by an ideal generated by homogeneous elements is used there without statement

proof.text: TensorAlgebra.gradedAlgebra gives an internal decomposition by T_n. For a finite zero relation in the comapped kernel grades, apply the injective subtype map and tensor-grade independence; each term is zero.

For x in the kernel, decompose x into its finite tensor components d_n and apply the quotient map. The resulting sum in the image grades is zero. Their independence, given by graded_image_internal, forces each image f(d_n) to be zero; components outside the support are zero as well. Thus the components lie in the kernel and span it. Apply DirectSum.isInternal_submodule_of_iSupIndep_of_iSup_eq_top.
